description: ClearanceKit: Managed and user-defined policy rules not enforced between opfilter start and first policy modification
how_introduced: AI-authored code contributed to this CVE. The original startup-order flaw was introduced in AI-coauthored commit 5a887953, which created XPCServer code that called applyPolicyToFilter() before the ES client existed, and AI-coauthored commit 614a7946 later reimplemented the same broken ordering in main.swift when initialization side effects were moved out of XPCServer.

bug_commits.author: Craig Bass
bug_commits.message: Merge daemon into opfilter as single privileged process

agent_verdicts.reasoning: This is the earliest commit that introduced the vulnerable startup design. It created XPCServer, had XPCServer.init load managed/user policy and immediately call applyPolicyToFilter(), and main instantiated XPCServer before calling adapter.start(initialRules: server.mergedRules()). Because ESInboundAdapter.updatePolicy returns early when client is nil, startup never reached interactor.updatePolicy(rules), so opfilter stayed on baseline faaPolicy until a later resync or policy modification.

bug_commits.author: Craig Bass
bug_commits.message: Move FileAuthPipeline and PolicyRepository construction to main.swift

agent_verdicts.reasoning: This commit moved initial policy application out of XPCServer.init and reimplemented it in main.swift as three explicit startup calls: server.applyPolicyToFilter(), server.applyAllowlistToFilter(), and server.applyJailRulesToFilter() before adapter.start(...). ESInboundAdapter.updatePolicy still had guard let client else { return }, so the startup policy apply became a no-op for policy state and interactor.updatePolicy(rules) never ran. That is exactly the broken initialization ordering fixed by 56d617.

ai_contribution: AI-authored code contributed to this CVE. The original startup-order flaw was introduced in AI-coauthored commit 5a887953, which created XPCServer code that called applyPolicyToFilter() before the ES client existed, and AI-coauthored commit 614a7946 later reimplemented the same broken ordering in main.swift when initialization side effects were moved out of XPCServer.
